summary: Hardens the wire-protocol reader against hostile or desynced backends: validates every backend message length and nested counts before allocating, bounds read-buffer growth at 32 MiB, fixes a quadratic C-string rescan, bounds GSS packet/token sizes, and fixes a skip() spin at EOF.

tests.evidence: Many new refusals had no off-by-one acceptance tests and no coverage of reuse after a refusal or GSS encrypted-path length check; later commits 901f887f26 and c346f3bb55 add them, and 5f2ee6b27c/ee1099eb98 fix tests that raced on CI (Windows, de_DE).

user_docs.evidence: No property or option added (deliberately knob-free); limits are user-visible only through the changelog, which is covered under change_description.

doc_comments.evidence: davecramer asked for comments explaining the NegotiateProtocolVersion guards; commit 5d0686ab96 notes MAX_SMALL_MESSAGE_LENGTH cited libpq's 30000 and 2000 'and was neither' (PGStream.java constant Javadoc).

change_description.evidence: vlsi: the changelog claim of preventing a two-gigabyte allocation is misleading since CopyData still allocates 1 GiB; vlsi CHANGES_REQUESTED to update the PR description; a later changelog entry stated the wrong SQLState (08006 vs 08S01).

performance.evidence: Touches the DataRow hot path, buffer growth and C-string scan; the buffer never shrank, so one 32 MiB message pinned memory per pooled connection (davecramer), fixed in 62f4a34726.

security.evidence: Parsing of untrusted network input is the PR's purpose; review found pre-auth ErrorResponse still allowed a 32 MiB allocation (4a9decdbab), unbounded GSS/auth round-trip loops (0993125bd2), and uncapped NegotiateProtocolVersion quadratic cost.

backward_compat.evidence: vlsi: libpq does not limit NoticeResponse, yet the PR kills long notices with no escape hatch; davecramer: a >32 MiB ErrorResponse from a large failing EXECUTE broke the connection. Fixed by truncation in 4ae88af22b.

concurrency.evidence: Connection lifecycle: a refused length left the desynced connection open for a pool to reuse (9163a35554 adds a broken flag, isClosed, SO_LINGER 0); davecramer later found the broken flag was not volatile and not checked on the read path (9ca108ce47).

error_model.evidence: New refusals throw plain IOException; pre-auth violations were retried under sslMode=allow/prefer instead of PSQLException 08P01 (fb8f245058); maxResultBuffer produced two chained exceptions with a misleading second cause (edbe901b94, davecramer 2026-09-16).

correctness.evidence: Dozens of per-message bounds and buffer arithmetic; copy response limit used Short.MAX_VALUE for an unsigned int2 (27c47b456e), RowDescription/ParameterDescription counts not cross-checked against the declared length.

user_value.evidence: vlsi questioned splitting attention from overlapping PR #4016, but the hardening itself is clearly valuable; not a new feature or API.

surprising_behavior.evidence: A legitimate large notice or error, or exceeding maxResultBuffer, now drops the connection; reviewers flagged the connection-fatal 32 MiB limit on server-sent text as unexpected.

contradictions.evidence: Changelog says a backend can no longer drive a gigabyte-scale allocation while CopyData/DataRow keep MaxAllocSize; the MAX_SMALL_MESSAGE_LENGTH comment cites libpq limits the value does not match.

build_ci.evidence: No build or CI files in the initial version; the CI flakiness came from the tests themselves.

observability.evidence: Error messages carry the offending lengths; the connection-drop path has no separate log, but the thrown exception is the signal.

spec_conformance.evidence: Each bound interprets the PostgreSQL protocol message layouts and libpq limits (VALID_LONG_MESSAGE_TYPE 30000, PQ_GSS_* sizes); the copy response bound treated an unsigned int2 as signed, and NoticeResponse/ErrorResponse limits diverged from libpq.

plan.why: A large security-sensitive protocol change with findings on many independent axes; focused reviewers for protocol bounds, compatibility/failure semantics, memory, tests, and prose.
